title: Notable physics papers on arXiv — Friday, 16 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending ranking. This is an inferred editorial shortlist, not a popularity chart; citation evidence is very limited for papers this new.

sections.title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
sections.abstract: The Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration reports a continuum-extrapolated lattice-QCD determination of the muon's leading-order hadronic vacuum-polarization contribution, with about 1% uncertainty.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain full HVP contribution aμ = (714.9 ± 8.1) × 10⁻¹⁰ after applying the WP25 leading isospin-breaking correction; they say the resulting Standard Model prediction is consistent with the latest Fermilab result and increases tension with pre-CMD-3 data-driven dispersive determinations.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; lattice QCD using ETMC Nf=2+1+1 gauge configurations, four lattice spacings, and a continuum extrapolation.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported full-HVP value combines the isospin-symmetric calculation with an external isospin-breaking correction; the comparison with dispersive results remains method-dependent and the paper does not settle the broader g−2 discrepancy.

sections.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
sections.abstract: Measurements in twisted bilayer WSe₂ identify an extended strange-metal regime in a partially filled Hubbard band and a superconducting dome emerging from that regime.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report an extended strange metal persisting to 100 mK across multiple symmetry-breaking ground states, only at small twist angles, and a new superconducting dome developing from it.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; transport observations in twisted bilayer WSe₂.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the observations favor an intrinsic strange-metal state, but that interpretation and its mechanism are not established beyond this material platform.

sections.title: First Observation of the Radiative Decay D⁰ → γω
sections.abstract: BESIII reports a 6.0σ observation of the radiative charm decay D⁰ → γω and measures its absolute branching fraction.
sections.claimed_result: From 20.3 fb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ data at 3.773 GeV, the authors report B(D⁰ → γω) = (2.12 ± 0.40(stat) ± 0.25(syst)) × 10⁻⁵ and interpret it as evidence for dominant long-distance hadronic dynamics in radiative charm decays.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; BESIII detector data, with a Particle Transformer-based analysis.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a single-experiment result; the interpretation as a benchmark for non-perturbative QCD depends on theoretical calculations and will benefit from independent scrutiny.

sections.title: Superconducting circuits host two-level systems with lifetimes exceeding one second
sections.abstract: Pump-probe spectroscopy of flux-tunable transmons identifies weakly coupled microscopic degrees of freedom with intrinsic lifetimes longer than one second.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer weak kilohertz-range coupling and lifetimes exceeding one second for microscopic degrees of freedom, identifying transmons as probes of such long-lived defects.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; wide-band quantum-jump correlation spectroscopy and detuning-dependent pump-probe measurements on flux-tunable transmons.
sections.unique_caveat: The data are consistent with positional defects described by the standard tunneling model, but the authors do not exclude magnetic spin impurities or trapped quasiparticles.

sections.title: A first look at the protoplanet WISPIT 2 b with VLTI/GRAVITY+
sections.abstract: New VLTI/GRAVITY+ astrometry and spectroscopy independently confirm WISPIT 2 b as a self-luminous, point-like companion within a young star's transitional disk.
sections.claimed_result: The authors detect the companion at about 322 mas, find a moderate-eccentricity orbit preferred by the new astrometry, estimate an effective temperature of 900–1300 K, and independently confirm it as a self-luminous point-like object at about 60 au.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; VLTI/GRAVITY+ astrometry and K-band spectrum, combined with VLT/SPHERE and literature photometry.
sections.unique_caveat: No circumplanetary disk is resolved; atmospheric properties remain weakly constrained, and the authors call for higher signal-to-noise or longer-wavelength observations.

sections.title: Band-Resolved Superconducting Gaps via the Thermal Hall Effect in CeRu₂
sections.abstract: Thermal Hall transport, constrained by specific heat and normal-state magnetotransport, is used to assign different superconducting gap magnitudes to electron and hole bands in CeRu₂.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer Δe/kB ≈ 13 K on heavy Ce 4f electron sheets and Δh/kB ≈ 8 K on hole sheets from a low-field sign reversal in κxy and a joint fit to thermal and normal-state transport constraints.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; thermal Hall transport, specific heat, and normal-state magnetotransport.
sections.unique_caveat: Band assignment is inferred through a constrained transport analysis rather than a direct band-by-band measurement, and the conclusion depends on the modelling of the electronic contributions.

sections.title: Gallium Anomaly and Solar Neutrinos
sections.abstract: The authors compare gallium solar-neutrino capture data with a solar-neutrino rate calibrated using neutrino–electron scattering and find agreement rather than an anomaly.
sections.claimed_result: The authors compare 66.1 ± 3.1 SNU from SAGE and Gallex/GNO with a solar-source strength of 67.5 +1.4/−1.1 SNU and conclude that the gallium result is not anomalous; they say neither the ⁷¹Ga charged-current cross section nor extraction/counting efficiencies explain the earlier anomaly.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; synthesis of gallium-source results and solar-neutrino constraints calibrated through neutrino–electron elastic scattering.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an inference from the comparison and its calibration inputs, not a new direct measurement of the original source experiments; the conclusion should be read in that analysis context.
